answer:
- NATO assigns three core tasks [C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8] to the Alliance in its Strategic Concept: deterrence and defence [C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C8]; crisis prevention and management [C1, C2, C3, C4, C8]; and cooperative security. [C1, C2, C3, C4]
- NATO's key purpose [C1, C2, C4] is to ensure collective defence [C1, C2, C4] based on a 360-degree approach. [C2, C4, C5, C6, C8]
- NATO's nuclear capability [C2, C4, C5, C6] is fundamental to preserving peace, preventing coercion and deterring aggression. [C2, C4]
- NATO's deterrence and defence posture [C5, C6] is based on an appropriate mix of nuclear, conventional and missile defence capabilities, complemented by space and cyber capabilities. [C5, C6]
- NATO will significantly strengthen its deterrence and defence posture [C2, C5, C6] to deny any potential adversary any possible opportunities for aggression. [C5, C6]
- NATO will continue to enhance the collective readiness, responsiveness, deployability, integration and interoperability of its forces. [C5, C6]
- NATO will individually and collectively deliver the full range of forces, capabilities, plans, resources, assets and infrastructure needed for deterrence and defence. [C5, C6]
- NATO will strengthen training and exercising, adapt and streamline its decision-making processes, enhance its planning and improve the effectiveness of its crisis response system. [C5, C6]
- NATO will continue to promote gender equality as a reflection of its values. [C1, C3, C6]
- NATO will continue to advance the Women, Peace and Security agenda across all its tasks. [C1, C2, C3, C6, C7]
